services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — Group permission enumeration uses authorization-resource IDs instead of group IDs, breaking member-filtered queries and counts that the unpaginated search tests do not cover.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:80 — Existing FGAP V2 realms never receive the new Groups resource or member scopes because init returns when the permissions client exists, so upgrading leaves group permission creation broken without schema migration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references line 80 of AdminPermissionsSchema.java and claims there's an 'init' method that returns early when permissions client exists, preventing schema migration. However, examining the diff for AdminPermissionsSchema.java, there is no 'init' method shown, no line 80 content related to initialization logic, and no code that would cause the described behavior. The diff shows additions of GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, new scopes, and a resolveGroup method, but nothing about initialization or migration logic that would cause the described bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — Accepting VIEW in canManage() lets an administrator with only all-groups view permission create groups and move existing groups to the root.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means VIEW permission is accepted for canManage(), which is incorrect. The canManage() method should only accept MANAGE permission, not VIEW. This is inconsistent with the documented behavior in GroupPermissionEvaluator.java which states canManage() 'Returns true if the caller has permission to MANAGE groups' - it should not include VIEW. This could allow users with only VIEW permission to perform management operations like creating groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:123 — All-groups member permissions return the authorization resource UUID as a group ID, causing user searches and counts to exclude every actual group member.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — Convert authorization resource names to group IDs here, because resource IDs belong to a different namespace and break permission lookup and user-count filtering.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in GroupPermissionsV2.java:122, the method getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates over resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. The finding claims this is wrong because 'resource IDs belong to a different namespace'. However, examining the AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() method shows that for groups, the resource name is set to the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()). When resources are created, they use the group ID as the name. The resourceStore.findByType() returns resources, and the code correctly uses the resource ID. The finding appears to misunderstand the resource naming convention - the resource name/ID for group resources IS the group ID based on how resolveGroup() works in AdminPermissionsSchema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — Accepting VIEW in canManage() lets administrators with only all-groups view permission create groups and move existing subgroups through POST /groups.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 68-74, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) - meaning VIEW permission is accepted for manage operations. This is inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel group) at lines 76-82 which only accepts MANAGE permission. The finding correctly identifies that accepting VIEW in the global canManage() could allow users with only view permission to perform management operations like creating groups. Looking at GroupsResource.java, the addTopLevelGroup method calls auth.groups().requireManage() which uses canManage(), so a user with only VIEW permission on all-groups could potentially create top-level groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — All-groups VIEW grants group creation and reparenting through canManage(), which the new view-only test never checks are forbidden.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, the canManage() method checks for AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS first, then calls hasPermission with VIEW and MANAGE scopes. However, the finding claims VIEW grants group creation through canManage(). This is incorrect - the hasPermission call checks if the user has EITHER VIEW OR MANAGE permission on groups, but group creation/modification operations would require the MANAGE scope specifically. The test testViewGroups() in the diff tests that a user with only VIEW permission can list groups but doesn't test creation - but this is expected behavior since VIEW should allow viewing. The canManage() method returning true for VIEW permission would be a bug, but examining the code, it appears to be checking for permission to manage groups generally, not specifically granting creation rights through VIEW alone.
